# libreac / fuzz_pcap

libreac's own fuzz target `fuzz_pcap` ([source](source/fuzz_pcap.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over libreac 1.9.0 (FreeREAC/libreac at d16f3f4e).

Reads the payload as a record-buffer capacity and a pcap file, which pcap_source_open opens through a stand-in for fopen that answers one path with fmemopen over a copy of that file. It reads every record that fits into a buffer of exactly that capacity (its own allocation), walking the file alongside the reader to know what each should be, then closes, reopens and reads the first record again without a timestamp, and closes once more.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static libreac.a of every src/*.c of libreac 1.9.0 at commit d16f3f4e, compiled with each build's flags, as libreac's Makefile builds its fuzz targets but with this toolchain in place of a native clang and libFuzzer.
- libreac's Makefile links this target with -Wl,--wrap=fopen, which collides with the sealed AddressSanitizer runtime's own __wrap_fopen. Instead, src/pcap_source.c is compiled a second time with -Dfopen=libreac_fuzz_fopen and the target with -D__wrap_fopen=libreac_fuzz_fopen -D__real_fopen=fopen, in all four builds, and that object is linked before libreac.a. No source file changes.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- Open accepts exactly a file of at least 24 bytes with one of the two classic magics, notes the byte order, and a reader that failed to open holds no stream ([lines 92-118](source/fuzz_pcap.c#L92-L118)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Each record handed back fits the buffer, is the file's next record that fits and is not empty, with the original length, and an 802.1Q tag stripped exactly when the record carries one, its VID kept; reading stops within one record per 16 bytes of file ([lines 132-203](source/fuzz_pcap.c#L132-L203)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The timestamp of each record handed back is the record header's seconds and microseconds ([lines 205-213](source/fuzz_pcap.c#L205-L213)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The walk ends with 0 exactly at the end of the file and with -1 on a cut record or header, never with any other answer ([lines 219-269](source/fuzz_pcap.c#L219-L269)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- After close the reader holds no stream and answers -1; it reopens, and the reopened reader gives the same first answer as before ([lines 273-295](source/fuzz_pcap.c#L273-L295)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libreac` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz_pcap.plain` | 49,336 | `1e8e7da32456ca11f5e70cba9413adf96bbeb09fb14d1c68e2a3c29a6cb0de01` |
| ubsan | `fuzz_pcap.ubsan` | 49,488 | `83af59086893b5608e2e6e71ea75e7355843d61ec2b20bf3fa1106f362b5e43f` |
| asan | `fuzz_pcap.asan` | 571,416 | `b7a91d9b1fb0017df0462bf382b3211837851bf801e792673b1cee0797cdca2a` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzz_pcap.asan-ubsan` | 571,112 | `9e66f771f22af67aadc8b8ddcd7ee91f46c4c63442c694faaf2375f9c5b79321` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
